failures.evidence: Red test (commit 5dffc26f): packages/pi-legion/extensions/legion.test.ts, test "/legion-controller-start run again while the start command's claim is in flight registers once and says nothing to do". Command: `cd packages/pi-legion && bun test ./extensions/legion.test.ts -t "run again while the start command"` -> 1 fail: the second run returns [] (it ran a whole second claim) where NOTHING_TO_DO is expected. Real-binary probe (throwaway, /legion/scratch/tmp/i511-zz-tester-probe.test.ts, a copy of controller-start-omp.test.ts's rig at 73dd84ff, Oh My Pi 18.12.2 under a PTY, real NATS): with the registration held, typing `/legion-controller-start` + Enter makes a second POST /legion/v1/claims/register (registrations while held: 2). With the stand-in giving each registration its own secret, as the daemon does (packages/daemon/internal/api/controller.go registerController: `secret := rand.Text()` and store.RegisterController replaces secret_hash each time), and the first claim's role claim answered 2 s late, the session keeps the first registration's secret: the start turn's `legion` set_status call got `POST /legion/v1/grants failed with 403: invalid controller secret` (grantSecrets=["secret-1"], current=secret-2, statusWrites=0). So a second run of the command during a slow claim can leave the controller unable to write any status until a re-claim. The same unserialised claim() is reached by /legion-claim-controller typed during the start command's claim (two registrations; in my one run it happened to finish in order and the grant was accepted). One start message was sent in every run; the defect is the second registration and the secret it can leave stale.
